🤨我靠！Claude Code / Codex / Pi 在同一模型上正确率差 1 个点，账单却差一倍。Pi 四个工具能打到帕累托前沿！

Berkeley 拿同一批模型，分别塞进 3 个外壳测：Claude Code、Codex、Pi

通俗对比：
🔹同一道题、同一个模型 Claude Code：对了 97.8%，花 $1.33 Pi：对了 96.7%，花 $0.67 多对 1 道题的零头，却多花一倍钱

🔹整体账单 Claude Code 大约是 Pi 的 2 倍，是 Codex 的 1.6 倍 Terminal 那组测试里，Claude Code 大约是 Pi 的 1.5 倍

🔹还有更夸张的 GPT-5.6 Sol 换到 Pi 上：分数更高，钱只要 Codex 的一半

🔹钱多花在哪了 两边跑的轮数几乎一样，但 Claude Code 一开口，塞给模型的说明就比 Pi 多 10 倍，等于每聊一轮，都先交一笔“外壳税”

一句话： 模型是发动机，外壳是车身。
 车身太厚，油耗先上去，速度不一定更快。
原生外壳也不一定最配。
 有的模型在 Pi 里更香，有的在 Codex 里更好。
 选模型时，把外壳一起比！

单张 GPU 每天狂刷 50 万页！法国 AI 团队最新发布的 LightOnOCR-2-1B 正在改写文档解析的成本法则：一个仅 1B（10 亿）参数的小模型，直接越级击败了体量为其 9 倍的竞争对手，并把海量文档处理成本拉低到每千页不到 1 美分。

传统 OCR 往往依赖脆弱的多阶段工程流水线（版面切分、文字检测、分块识别再到后处理拼接），任何环节出错都会导致阅读顺序错乱。而该模型采用纯端到端设计，输入任意 PDF、扫描件或照片，模型直出规整、顺序正确的结构化文本。

核心亮点：

极致吞吐与超低成本：单张 H100 跑出 5.71 页/秒的速度，单卡单日吞吐量约 49.3 万页，每千页处理成本低于 $0.01。

越级 SOTA 性能：在 OlmOCR-Bench 基准测试中达到业界领先水准，而体量比同台竞技的竞品小约 9 倍；推理速度相比 Chandra 快 3.3 倍、相比 dots.ocr 快 5 倍、相比 OlmOCR 快 1.7 倍。

复杂版面全兼容：精准处理多栏排版、跨行表格、各类单据与表单，数学公式直接输出规范整洁的 LaTeX 语法。

开箱即用与本地部署：覆盖 11 种语言，原生兼容高吞吐框架 vLLM 与 SGLang，也支持在 Ollama 或 LM Studio 本地轻量运行。

真开源商用：采用宽松的 Apache 2.0 协议，企业二次开发和商业落地全无门槛。

无论是需要清洗海量 PDF 构建 RAG 知识库，还是搭建自动化单据录入管线，这个小钢炮模型都把算力利用率拉到了新高度：https://t.co/RYicLVBm76

So I’ve decided I’m done making content about Sebbywebz and the people around him.

One thing I’ve learned in life is that hate and aggression do not sustain themselves forever. They take a toll. Watching the videos, reading the tweets, dealing with the arguments, and even seeing the same rhetoric spill into unrelated comment sections has taken enough of a toll on me mentally. I’ve noticed I have been more miserable and just plain burnt out.

Throwing around labels like “shills,” “fanatics,” and all the other heinous wording does not make everyone else look bad. Eventually, it makes YOU look bad. I drew the line at seeing someone say, “I hope this sells 0 copies.” That, to me, is a state of misery I will never get to.

At some point, you have to ask yourself: what is the goal? If the goal is to make a game fail, reduce its sales, or make other people miserable for enjoying it, what are you actually accomplishing?

Taking shots at other creators and invading other communities is childish. You are not, and never will be, the authority on the Final Fantasy series. Having that experience in that Discord proved to me everything I suspected.

I think of hate like coffee. Having a lot of it gives you a quick jolt and keeps you going for a while, but eventually the effect wears off, you crash, you get a migraine, and you need more just to feel the same thing, to get rid of those effects. Round and Round we go. 

You are a 40-year-old man acting like a 12-year-old. Grow. Up.

Then I asked MYSELF, “Why am I doing this?” I couldn’t answer it, and that’s not a good thing.

Sooner or later, people get exhausted by it.

I also want to apologize to all the folks who have seen my tweets about him. It’s not fair to you, and most of all, the fans here. I want to be more positive and, most of all, happy going forward.

I am so honored and happy to be part of a fandom like this. Games like this make me feel like a kid again, which I think we all need in our lives.

I almost fell into the same obsessive trap. Thanks to all the people I met and the friends I made along the way.

To a better and more positive future.

I've spent $2k to $3k a month on @UberEats @Uber $UBER  since the app first launched. I was Platinum until they killed the tiers.

Everyone knows restaurants mess up orders. When you are sitting at the restaurant, it does not matter. You tell the waiter, they fix it.

When it is delivery, you live with whatever bag shows up at your door. That is exactly why a refund process for missing or wrong items has to be frictionless.

For years it was. It took seconds.

Not anymore.

Last week I ordered baklava. What arrived looked nothing like baklava. I opened a case for wrong item, sent photos, got denied. Quote, item cannot be refunded.

Last night an item was missing from our order. Same story. It used to be resolved instantly. This time it took seven hours to get a reply saying sorry, without photos we cannot review the case. How do you photograph an item that never arrived?

When there is no customer protection, the entire convenience disappears.

I have been loyal for years, but I am seriously looking at @DoorDash now.

Jev can only choose from the options you give it. I think that limitation shows us where the harder problem starts.

That was the part of @0xcodila’s piece on @typesafeai’s Jev that stayed with me.

You give Jev a state and a finite answer space. It returns a probability distribution. If something relevant exists in reality but has not yet been identified, named, or represented, there is no concrete option for Jev to judge.

Once it has been turned into a clear enough input, the situation changes. A vague question becomes a bounded judgment.

At the smallest scale, Jev almost feels like an atomic form of intelligence. I do not mean that it understands the whole world. I mean that if a question has been made sufficiently atomic, it can make a probabilistic judgment about something real.

The problem is that open-ended questions do not arrive in this form.

Some of what matters may already exist, but we have not learned to see it. Sometimes we are using the wrong categories. Sometimes the relevant relationship has no name yet. Before it is defined, it is almost suspended: real, possibly decisive, but without a form the system can operate on.

Frontier models are useful for this part. They can explore different ways of framing the problem, generate candidates, reorganize scattered information, or create a structure that was not present in the original question. More models, agents and compute can help if they expand the search without losing the ability to filter and integrate.

Jev does almost the opposite. It becomes useful after some part of that space has taken form. Then probability can constrain what would otherwise remain another plausible piece of generated language.

The obvious description would be: the LLM discovers, and Jev judges. I think the real relationship is less clean. A judgment can expose a missing option. A new option can change the representation. The new representation can make the original question look different.

So I do not think the important object is either model by itself. It is the movement between two states: something unknown but real, and something defined enough to be judged.

How much intelligence can be built out of that movement?

If you have a website, stop indexing your pages one at a time.

Most people go to Google Search Console, paste in their URL, and request indexing. One page, one click, over and over. Here's how to get Google to see it in about 24 hours instead.

Type in site colon and then your website. That shows you every page Google actually sees. Google can't rank pages it hasn't found.

If any of your pages aren't showing up there, do this.

Copy the link. Type in SpeedyIndex and click the first one. Go to Create task, scroll down, put your link in, and hit Create. You can drop a whole list of URLs in at once.

This tells Google the page actually exists instead of waiting a week or more for Google to get around to crawling it on its own.

Found faster, results sooner. That's the whole tip.

Send this to whoever runs your website. [ You can also have claude build you one]
